headline: Leafs’ Marshall Rifai placed on IR, week-to-week with lower-body injury
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Toronto defenseman Marshall Rifai has been placed on injured reserve and is week-to-week with a lower-body injury. He sat out Thursday's 5-4 win over the Rangers after he was "dealing with something" during the morning skate.

The sample is tiny, but Rifai's numbers so far this season are worth a note. In two games he has one goal, yet the quality of his own chances (expected goals) works out to just 0.07, so he is about 0.93 goals ahead of what those chances would normally produce. That points to a finisher running hot rather than a new source of offense. At five-on-five, Toronto has taken only 28 percent of the expected goals with him on the ice, and the team's share is 15.7 percentage points better when he isn't out there. The Leafs as a whole sit at 43 percent at five-on-five, so they are being outplayed even before this injury. Going by how the coach has used his players, Nick Blankenburg (13:25 a night) is next in line for Rifai's minutes, which currently run 14:09 a night and include time on the second power-play unit.
